record.paper_title: Open problems for the superKdV equations
record.original_question: Explain why the N = 2 supersymmetric KdV equation SKdV_1 has the first fermionic conservation laws but does not generate infinite towers of fermionic conservation laws, in contrast with the a = -2 and a = 4 cases.

evidence.quote: On the other hand, for the a = 1 case, the first fermionic laws (3.9) do not generate infinite towers: they are isolated. OP-4: Why there are no infinite towers of fermionic conservation laws for SKdV1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-parameter family of N=2 supersymmetric Korteweg–de Vries equations
  Φ_t = −Φ_{xxx} + 3(Φ D_1 D_2 Φ)_x + ½(a−1)(D_1 D_2 Φ^2)_x + 3a Φ^2 Φ_x,
where Φ(x,t,θ_1,θ_2) is an N=2 superboson superfield depending on a bosonic variable x, time t, and two Grassmann (anticommuting) variables θ_1, θ_2, and where D_i = ∂_{θ_i} + θ_i ∂_x are the standard super-derivatives (so that D_i^2 = ∂_x and D_1 D_2 + D_2 D_1 = 0). For exactly three values of the real parameter a, namely a ∈ {−2, 1, 4}, this equation is known to admit a first nontrivial fermionic conservation law.

For a = −2 and a = 4 (the cases known to be completely integrable in the standard sense), the first fermionic conservation law sits inside an infinite tower of independent fermionic conservation laws of increasing differential order, generated by an appropriate recursion operator or Lax structure.

For a = 1 (the SKdV_1 equation), in contrast, although the equation possesses a first fermionic conservation law of the same general type, this law is isolated: no infinite tower of independent fermionic conservation laws based on it is presently known.

Problem. Provide a structural explanation for the following phenomenon: identify the mechanism (Lax/recursion/Hamiltonian/cohomological) responsible for the fact that the a = 1 case of the N=2 super KdV family admits its first fermionic conservation laws as isolated objects, i.e. they do not generate an infinite hierarchy of fermionic conservation laws, while in the a = −2 and a = 4 cases such infinite towers do exist. Equivalently, prove or disprove the existence of an infinite tower of independent fermionic conservation laws for the a = 1 N=2 super KdV equation.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that while the a=1 (SKdV_1) case has been studied — including its Painlevé property, bilinear form, Bäcklund transformation, soliton solutions and a bi-Hamiltonian structure with associated nonlocal/nonpolynomial bosonic and fermionic symmetries — no result establishes an infinite tower of fermionic conservation laws generated by the first fermionic law, nor a definitive structural obstruction explaining its isolation. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Bi-Hamiltonian structure of the N=2 supersymmetric α=1 KdV hierarchy
status_evidence.snippet: new nonpolynomial and nonlocal, bosonic and fermionic symmetries and Hamiltonians, with bi-Hamiltonian structure and recursion relations
status_evidence.claim: Symmetry/Hamiltonian structures for the a=1 case have been investigated but the question of an infinite tower of fermionic conservation laws is not resolved there.

status_evidence.title: The Painlevé analysis for N = 2 super KdV equations
status_evidence.snippet: SKdV1 case is one of the integrable supersymmetric KdV equations passing the Painlevé test
status_evidence.claim: SKdV_1 is studied as integrable in the Painlevé sense, yet the fermionic-tower question is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Higher order supersymmetries and fermionic conservation laws of the supersymmetric extension of the KdV equation
status_evidence.snippet: Hierarchies of fermionic conservation laws for super KdV
status_evidence.claim: Infinite hierarchies of fermionic conservation laws are known in integrable cases (a=-2, 4), contrasting with the isolated nature in the a=1 case.
